the development of a working environment for a user to prepare and analyze precise descriptions of the system being developed, to execute and simulate them, and to generate running code from them.

the design and construction of a computer-aided environment that supports the development of complex, real-time reactive systems from the early stages of analysis and design, through detailed design, implementation, and testing, all the way to the final maintenance and documentation.
the development of a new methodology for the design of reactive systems, based on the use of statecharts.

STATEMATE is the first system of its kind, which provides a complete and integrated working environment for the design and implementation of complex reactive systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

STATEMATE is a powerful, yet user-friendly, environment for the development and analysis of complex reactive systems, which can be used to develop systems of considerable size, and which can be used in conjunction with other CASE tools to form an integrated environment.
a graphical working environment for complex reactive systems can and should be a full-scale, fully integrated, and fully automated environment, rather than a collection of loosely connected tools.
a system that is designed in STATEMATE is automatically transformed into executable code.
